newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 1.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc and ADT Ltd agreed to cancel Republic's proposed $4.49 billion purchase of ADT. The deal seemingly fell apart after ADT tried to change it as Republic's stock fell, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday.

* The job guarantees that Ford Motor Co and Chrysler Corp gave to the United Auto workers include previously undisclosed escape clauses that could help General Motors Corp accept similar guarantees in a new labor contract.
* Retail prices for used cars and light trucks have been falling in recent months in a trend that auto industry experts say usually means trouble for sales of new vehicles.
* August new home sales rose 4.7 percent to the highest annual rate in over a decade. Personal spending and income each rose 0.6 percent during the same month.
* Banks that specialize in credit cards are bolstering their pitches to consumers while traditional banks are slowing down, signaling a shift in the business of selling consumer debt.
* Revco DS Inc sued Big B Inc to block a shareholder rights plan that Big B installed after Revco launched its $330 million hostile takeover bid.
* The Dow industrials gained 227.54 or 4.0 percent during the third quarter, while stock and bond offerings rose 5.4 percent to $205.3 billion.
* Merrill is losing ground in municipal-bond underwriting in the wake of its battle with Orange County, California.
* IVAX Corp expects to report a $43 million loss for the third quarter, including an $8 million restructuring charge.
* Morton International Inc agreed to merge its airbag business with Sweden's Autoliv, while keeping its salt and chemical lines.
* Mead Corp has agreed to acquire a paper mill and woodlands from Boise Cascade Corp for about $650 million.
* The NASD shelved a proposal to assign "risk ratings" for bond funds, despite the Securities and Exchange Commission's interest in the plan.
* EchoStar Communications Corp DISH.O is negotiating with telephone giant Sprint Corp to create an alliance in the direct-broadcast satellite television market.
* New England will sell most of its power assets.
* Kiwi International Air Lines filed for bankruptcy protection in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Newark, N.J.

* Banc One is sitting out the latest round of bank mergers and focusing on cost cutting and consolidation. But some analysts fear that it may want to make an expensive acquisition to dilute earnings and lower the price of its stock.

* Economic data showing strength in the manufacturing and housing sectors sparked concern in the bond market that the U.S. Federal Reserve needed to slow down econopmic growth by raising short-term interest rates.
